thread:
mohit: heads up — our int8 canary that rolled yesterday showed a 3.8% spike in structured-output parse failures for the toolcall bench. noticed during the midnight sweep. canary-bot: canary report posted: https://infradash/redwood/canaries/17285 — spike started ~00:12 UTC, peaked at 00:28 :chart_with_upwards_trend:
sasha: ugh. any obvious diff in the prompt payload or tokenizer stats?
mohit: preliminary: same prompts, same schemas. quant config changed: per-layer asym int8 + aggressive activation clipping. also changed batching window (50ms -> 30ms) on the canary pool.
elaine: parse failure sample (copied from logs):
```
ERROR: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
RESPONSE SNIPPET: "\u0000\u0000\u0000\"{\"action\":\"create_ticket\",\"args\": {\"title\": \"...\"}"```
looks like leading control bytes in a handful of responses.
derek: control bytes often from tokenization/encoding mismatch or streaming boundary corruption. did we change streaming chunk framing?
mohit: not intentionally. runtime logs show a small increase in chunk-size variance after batch window tweak.
sasha: could be kv-cache / prefix trimming interacting with quantized model producing NULs for some first tokens. we saw similar with a different model months ago.
elaine: I ran 30 failing samples through the full token inspection. pattern: failures concentrated on short responses with toolcall JSON starting at token boundary. the model sometimes emits a leading 0x00 or 0x03 controlchar before "{".
canary-bot: alert details: failure mode = streaming-prefix-noise, affected model = raven-int8-v3q-canary-17285, failure-rate=3.8%, baseline=0.2%
mohit: action items I propose:
- roll back batch window to 50ms on the canary pool (temp)
- add streaming scrub that drops leading control chars before parse attempt
- add token-level logging for 1% sample to trace boundary alignment
- run microbench of kv-cache off vs on for same prompts
sasha: +1 for scrub as an immediate mitigation. can we make scrub idempotent and cheap? simple regex to remove leading controlchars (<=0x1F) before json parse should work.
derek: agree for scrub. but we need root cause — if quantization leads to occasional controlchar tokens at sequence start, that's a quality regression we should mark. add a test in onboarding harness: detect any non-printable prefix in generated strings across N samples.
elaine: I'll draft the scrub PR and patch the canary runtime to enable log-capture for scrubbed outputs (so we can compare raw vs cleaned).
mohit: who can run kv-cache microbench? sasha?
sasha: I can run it — will compare with 10k calls, kv on vs kv off, both canary int8 and baseline fp16. will share notebook. ETA EOD PST.
derek: add to postmortem checklist: "quantize-canary-struct-output-regression" with tags: int8, streaming, kvcache, batch-window. we should also add a gating check in the quant onboarding pipeline: structured-output-parse-fail-rate must be <= baseline + 0.5%.
mohit: timeline: rollback batch window now, scrub deploy in 30m, run kv microbench in parallel, follow up 9:30am PT standup with results.
elaine: scrub PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/7421 — includes unit test that strips \u0000 and other control chars pre-parse.
canary-bot: deploy started for scrub flag on canary pool. commit=a1b2c3, duration est=5m.
sasha: kv microbench notes (early): int8 has slightly higher entropy on first token distribution for these prompts — small but noticeable shift toward low-value tokens that map to control chars under current encoding table. full run in progress.
derek: if kv-cache amplifies the pattern we may need to adjust prefix-encodings or add a noop token guard early in the stream for quant models.
mohit: appreciate the quick cycle. let's keep this thread for retro notes. we'll convert to a short postmortem after we have kpv bench + canary scrub metrics. :thumbsup:
